    ATS Resume Checker Guide: 12 Formatting Rules That Pass Applicant Tracking Systems

    By ATS Score Checker Free Editorial TeamUpdated October 31, 2026 10 min read

    Formatting is the part of resume writing that feels least important and causes the most ATS problems. The good news: it is also the easiest to fix. These twelve rules come from the issues an ATS resume checker flags most often. Apply them once, save the result as your master resume, and every tailored version you create afterwards inherits a clean structure.

    Layout and structure

    1. Use a single-column layout

    One column, left-aligned, top to bottom. This is the single biggest improvement for most resumes, because it guarantees the reading order the software sees matches the order you intended.

    2. Use standard section headings

    Stick to recognisable labels: Summary, Experience (or Work Experience), Education, Skills, Certifications, Projects. You can style them in bold or a slightly larger size; just keep the words conventional.

    3. Order sections by relevance

    Experienced candidates: Summary → Experience → Skills → Education. Students and recent graduates: Summary → Education → Projects → Experience → Skills. Career changers can lead with a Skills or Relevant Projects section to put transferable ability up front.

    4. Keep contact details in the body

    Your name, phone, email, city/region and LinkedIn URL should sit as plain text at the very top of page one, not inside the document's header or footer area. Skip your full street address; city and country are enough.

    Text and typography

    5. Choose a common font

    Arial, Calibri, Helvetica, Georgia, Garamond and Cambria are all safe. Use 10–12pt for body text and 14–16pt for your name. Decorative or icon fonts can map to the wrong characters when extracted.

    6. Use simple bullets

    Standard round bullets or hyphens parse reliably. Custom symbols, arrows, emoji and check-mark icons sometimes turn into question marks or disappear.

    7. Write skills as words, not graphics

    Progress bars, star ratings and pie charts look tidy but contain no readable text. Replace them with a plain list, grouped if helpful: "Languages: Python, SQL, TypeScript · Tools: Airflow, dbt, Tableau".

    8. Spell out acronyms once

    Recruiters might search for either form. Write "Customer Relationship Management (CRM)" the first time, then use CRM. The same goes for certifications: "Project Management Professional (PMP)".

    Dates, titles and details

    9. Keep dates consistent

    Pick one format and use it everywhere: "Jun 2022 – Present". Place dates on the same line as the job title or directly below it, in the same position for every role. Consistency helps the parser link each date range to the right job.

    10. Give every role the same structure

    Job Title — Company, City — Dates, followed by 3–6 bullets. When each entry follows the same pattern, both software and people can scan it quickly.

    Files and submission

    11. Submit a text-based PDF or DOCX

    Export your PDF directly from Word, Google Docs or a similar editor so the text layer is preserved. Avoid scanned PDFs and design-tool exports that convert text to shapes. If the application asks for a specific format, follow it.

    12. Use a clear file name

    "Priya-Sharma-Data-Analyst-Resume.pdf" is better than "resume_final_v7.pdf". It does not change your ATS score, but recruiters download and forward files, and a clear name looks professional.

    Checklist

    • Single column, no tables or text boxes
    • Standard headings: Summary, Experience, Education, Skills
    • Contact details as text at the top of the body
    • Common font, 10–12pt body text
    • Plain bullets, no icons or graphics carrying information
    • Acronyms spelled out once
    • One consistent date format
    • Text-based PDF or DOCX with a clear file name

    Frequently asked questions

    Should an ATS-friendly resume be one page?

    Length is less important to an ATS than structure. As a guideline, one page suits early-career candidates and two pages suits most experienced professionals. Senior or academic roles can justify more.

    Can I use bold and italics?

    Yes. Bold, italics and simple horizontal lines are safe. Avoid text boxes, tables used for layout, images and graphics that carry information.

    Are resume templates ATS-friendly?

    Some are, many are not. Run any template through an ATS resume checker before using it and check that the plain-text output reads in the correct order.
